# VS Code Extension API

The TypeScript surface an editor extension is written against: contribution points declared in
`package.json`, an `activate(ctx)` entry point, and a `vscode` module available only inside the
extension host. In [[agent-orchestrator]] it is 573 lines whose entire job is to spawn a Python
subprocess, forward JSON, and host a webview.

## The parts that carry weight

- **`registerWebviewViewProvider` and `createWebviewPanel`** — the sidebar view and the wide Activity
  panel are two hosts for **one** HTML file, so both surfaces are registered against the same set of
  live webviews and every event is broadcast to all of them
  ([[self-contained-single-file-html]]).
- **`ctx.secrets`** — encrypted SecretStorage, which is where an [[openrouter]] key belongs. Reached
  first, with the plaintext settings field as a fallback the panel offers to migrate
  ([[secrets-from-environment-only]]).
- **`workspace.getConfiguration` / `ConfigurationTarget.Global`** — settings are read per run, and
  the autonomy toggle in the panel writes back through the same API rather than keeping its own copy.
- **`workspace.workspaceFolders`** — the open folder is what the backend and both CLIs are given as
  their working directory. No folder open is a real state, not an assertion failure.
- **`localResourceRoots`** — the webview may load from `media/` and nowhere else.

## The constraint that shapes everything else

**A `WebviewView` is destroyed whenever the user switches to another view container** — Explorer,
Source Control — and rebuilt with an empty DOM on return. Nothing in the DOM survives; anything the
panel wants back it must be re-sent. That single fact produced [[replay-a-recorded-run]], and it is
worth knowing before designing a sidebar rather than after a bug report.

## What is deliberately not used

No `LanguageModel` API, no chat participant, no task provider. The extension owns no orchestration
logic at all — it is a shell around a subprocess ([[drive-the-clis-not-the-apis]]), and it ships with
**zero runtime dependencies** and no bundler ([[zero-dependency-no-build-step]]).

Packaging is `vsce` producing a `.vsix`; the manifest's `contributes` block is the only place
commands, settings and views exist, which is why a test asserts every contributed command is actually
registered — [[tests-that-guard-the-repository]].
